source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Note the date and time of the inspection.
3. Document the location of the building, including the address, city, and state.
4. Record the name of the inspector(s) and their credentials, if applicable.
5. Clearly state whether the inspection was scheduled or conducted as part of a random check.
6. Detail the purpose of the inspection (e.g., a routine accessibility audit, complaint response, new construction compliance check, etc.)
7. Reference any relevant laws or standards that the building was evaluated against (e.g., the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), state-specific building codes, local ordinances, etc.)
8. List all areas and features within the building that were inspected (e.g., entrances, exits, pathways, restrooms, parking spaces, signage, seating, etc.)
9. Identify each failed check item by describing the deficiency precisely and how it does not comply with the required laws or standards.
10. Provide measurable details for each
